dimensions.note: The extension accepts no credentials, marks outbox payloads sensitive, and warns against embedding tokens in non-sensitive URL configuration.
Structured logs cover entry, success, HTTP failure, and network failure without payloads or idempotency keys.
The outbox adapter throws before writing on network and non-2xx failures so the caller can own retry state; the legacy send method retains its documented audit-record behavior.
Thirteen tests cover schemas, boundaries, HTTP success/failure, redaction, replay semantics, runtime-injected configuration, and topic encoding.
At-least-once semantics and the lack of provider-side deduplication are explicit; the outbox caller owns deduplication and retries.
Requests use bounded schemas, encoded topic path segments, a 30-second timeout, status checks, and bounded status-text diagnostics.
Fetch is timeout-bounded and failure responses are not read into unbounded memory.
The additive adapter is transport-specific, documented, and does not alter the existing send method.
Payload and option objects are strict and bounded; only the two known Swamp runtime-injected model configuration fields are tolerated.
Notification audit records have a seven-day lifetime and bounded garbage collection.
This transport model sends notifications and records attempts; it does not own a remote CRUD resource.
The provider exposes no separate non-mutating validation endpoint; strict input validation and bounded HTTP execution are used.
Both methods write the same notification schema and use timestamp-plus-UUID names to avoid concurrent collisions.
The model writes only its own notification audit resource and does not query unrelated model data.
The additive 2026.08.23.1 upgrade preserves existing attributes and the legacy send method.
